title: Join hands to provide clean water to schools affected by drought and saltwater intrusion
description:
With local response and other support sources, the Vietnam Children's Fund calls for the cooperation of the UnityGive user community to equip 2 Kindergartens (out of 12 schools benefiting from the project) with water filters and water tanks.  Specifically:

1. Thoi Thanh kindergarten

2. Thanh Phong kindergarten

General project information:

In recent times, the drought and saltwater intrusion have persisted and penetrated deep into the interior of Ben Tre province, greatly affecting the daily lives of people, especially children in the province. Salinity intrusion in 2023 - 2024 affected 10/13 provinces in the Mekong Delta region, the salinity boundary of 4 grams/liter affected 42.5% of the natural area of ​​the entire region, equivalent to 1,688,600 hectares, 50,376 hectares higher than in 2021. Drought, lack of water for daily irrigation, and saltwater intrusion have affected about 6,650 hectares in six provinces of the region, of which Ben Tre province is the most heavily affected province, affecting crop productivity, with about 355 hectares of trees damaged and completely lost. Drought and saltwater intrusion have caused 1,241 hectares of crops in the provinces to lack irrigation water, of which 541 hectares were completely damaged. Aquaculture in Ben Tre province also suffered more severe damage, including traditional fish farming, brackish water shrimp farming,...

The negative impact of the epidemic on some areas is still ongoing, which has a great impact on the lives of people, especially children. Drought and saltwater intrusion have also affected about 96,000 households, equivalent to about 430,000 people are living in 06 coastal provinces of the Mekong Delta region, of which Ben Tre province is the most affected province in the region, with a serious lack of domestic water, including 20,600 households in the water supply area from centralized water supply works, 75,400 households in the household water supply area. The cause of lack of water for daily use in the dry season this year is due to water sources at water supply works and saltwater intrusion deep into the field. Nguồn nước mặt bị nhiễm mặn, nguồn nước ngầm suy giảm, nhân dân sử dụng nước ngọt từ việc tích trữ nước mưa trong lu, khạp và bể chứa nước …

Faced with that situation, disadvantaged groups in the province are heavily affected, especially school-age children who have been affected by the recent prolonged drought and saltwater intrusion.

The project was formed to meet one of the practical requirements of students, especially children in Thanh Phu district. This is one of the favorable conditions to help care for and nurture children in the community better, their health is more assured so they can access education in the best way.

The Education and Training Sector of Thanh Phu district includes 1,540 teachers and staff with 24,364 students at 60 schools of 4 educational levels (18 preschools, kindergartens; 19 primary schools, 18 junior high schools, 4 high schools and 1 continuing education center - vocational education). Most students live and study in difficult and difficult conditions. Struggling because of roads and travel conditions, many students live in aquaculture areas or in fields growing crops, quite far from the central school; For schools in hamlets, you have to cross rivers and canals to get to school. Eating, drinking, studying, and taking care of children's health when they go to school are still not given proper attention by families and schools, affecting the physical and mental development of students.

title: Find Bao Thy's smile again
description:

Baby Bao Thy is the youngest stepchild in a poor farmer family. My parents, Mr. Kim and Mrs. Khe, work in the fields to raise three young children. The place where they live is in the poor remote commune of Cu San (M'Drak district, Dak Lak province), which is often flooded, crops fail, and the family is always in a state of hunger, causing little Thy's health to deteriorate further.

Baby Thy has been treated by the Dak Lak Tu Tam Association for nearly 2 years, but the tumor on her face is still growing larger, pulling her eyes, nose, ears, and mouth askew, causing pain and making all of her daily activities extremely difficult. However, little Thy is still hard-working, eager to learn, sociable with friends and knows how to help her mother with housework and taking care of her younger siblings.

Bao Thy was twice awarded a special scholarship by the Dak Lak Tu Tam Association because of her will to rise and strong determination. Every time I receive a scholarship, I am very happy, but I cannot smile fully. Her dream is to be able to smile as beautifully as her peers. The baby's treatment process is still very long and requires a lot of funding to help him regain his childhood smile.

title: Intellectual Bridge Scholarship
description:
Intellectual Bridge is a charity scholarship project established to create conditions for poor children in Dai Loc District, Quang Nam Province to go to school through direct and genuine contributions with the goal of supporting the entire time the students are in school. From 2011 until now, the project has supported nearly 500 students to overcome difficulties and achieve remarkable academic results such as: receiving a full 7-year dental scholarship in Russia, a full scholarship to Japan for 1 year...

We believe that a solid educational foundation is the key to success, helping poor students reach success. Through this project, benefactors can make contributions, big or small, to help students complete their learning path.

Current situation?

Dai Loc is a difficult district of Quang Nam province with more than 11 thousand poor households, including more than 3 thousand poor students and 1,200 students in extremely difficult circumstances.

The schools with students supported by the project are schools with a majority of poor students, located in communes on the outskirts of Dai Loc. Every year, these communes often have to suffer natural disasters such as droughts and floods, so despite their best efforts, people are still poor due to crop failure, lack of jobs, etc. However, the children's spirit of learning and overcoming difficulties is very great. Most of the children who received help passed admission to universities and colleges in big cities.

Support goals in 2023 - 2024?

In the 2023 - 2024 school year, the project hopes to continue supporting about 40 students at three schools that the project has accompanied for the past 11 years, including:

Scholarship value: 2.5 million/year/student including all necessary learning materials for a school year (textbooks, uniforms, school bags, paper, pens, hats, shoes); and all regular and extracurricular tuition, insurance costs, etc. will be paid directly so that children can feel secure in going to school.

How to choose and support?

Each year, the project has several surveys to visit students' families and check their learning. This work is actively supported by the Board of Directors of the schools where the children study and at the same time under the agreement of the Dai Loc District Learning Promotion Association. The selection criteria is that poor students overcome difficulties in learning from middle school, high school and university. For children who do not have results according to the project's criteria, the project will stop helping those children in the following school years.

Results and achievements?

* High school level:

Thanks to the scholarship program, most students make progress in their studies. From the beginning, there were no good students. Now, most of them have achieved quite good results. Some children are still at an average level due to knowledge gaps when they do not have the conditions to study. 100% of high school students pass graduation. More than 70% of high school graduates continue to study at college and university.

* University:

All of them have had quite good results throughout their years in college. College students all have part-time jobs after school to earn money. Especially, there is a job to do during summer vacation.

One student in this program, thanks to his excellent academic performance, received a full scholarship to study medicine in Russia. One student won a place to study abroad in Japan for 1 year. An excellent graduate in Auditing, currently working for a Dutch Auditing company.

What the project has done in recent years has only met a small part of the need to help children in extremely difficult circumstances in Dai Loc District, so through the UnityGive platform, the project hopes to receive the support of friends and organizations for the children of Quang Trung Secondary School, in order to help many poor students have the conditions to go to school and realize their dreams.

During the project, the children experienced practical lessons, a minimalist lifestyle, enough love and connection between members from other provinces. Access to education is a child's privilege, the door that opens the horizon of knowledge for humanity. However, the fact that thousands of children drop out of school due to economic inadequacy is still an ominous reality for future preschoolers. Especially in rural and mountainous areas, when meals still have to be taken care of every day, going to school is only  in children's dreams. The project does not stop at short-term support but throughout 6 years of schooling to help improve project effectiveness and create a strong change in the children's future.

"Raising Children Joining Hands for the Community" is the desire to create a sustainable and long-term relationship between the donor and the recipient like family members.

title: A thousand kites give hope
description:
Help many pediatric patients with the "Kite of Hope" Fundraising Campaign

. We would like to call for the help of the community of UnityGive donors to raise funds for 1,000 kites, equivalent to 380,000,000 VND for the Kite of Hope Campaign.

Urgent medical needs for children

According to the most recent statistics from health authorities, each year Vietnam has about 41,000 children with birth defects. This rate is equivalent to a child with a birth defect being born every 13 minutes. Among them, about 1,400-1,800 children have Down syndrome, 1,000-1,500 children have neural tube defects, 300-400 children have congenital hypothyroidism, about 2,200 children have hemolytic anemia... This number does not include children suffering from accidents and diseases due to external factors.

Medical costs for families who unfortunately encounter the above situations are huge. Therefore, since 2006, the Raising Children's Foundation was founded to provide specialized medical and surgical treatment expertise according to international standards for children with birth defects in difficult circumstances. This organization was born with the mission of creating the power of love, helping children in difficult circumstances across Vietnam overcome physical defects through methodical medical treatment, and have the opportunity to develop their full potential for a new, better life.

During 19 years of operation in Vietnam, the Children's Advancement Fund has helped more than 870 children with birth defects and injuries due to accidents access treatment at the best medical facilities in Vietnam thanks to the contributions of domestic and foreign businesses and philanthropists. Fundraising resources are used to fully support the entire treatment process, from surgery until the children recover from their disabilities (including travel and accommodation costs for relatives who care for the patient).

General diseases and surgeries that have been supported by the Elevate Childhood Fund include: Retinoblastoma (Eye cancer), infant retinal detachment, ROP, eye, maxillofacial, congenital cardiovascular diseases, vascular diseases, orthopedic injuries, urology, digestion, neurology and other special cases due to accidents or diseases such as burns and disabilities caused by polio.

"Kite of Hope" Festival

Summer is a time for children to have fun, explore and experience meaningful activities. However, this legitimate right is a distant dream for children who are unfortunately sick or have accidents. This is the motivation for the Raising Children's Fund to deploy the campaign and organize the charity fundraising festival "Kite of Hope" to mobilize resources from individuals and organizations through diverse and practical activities.

Ms. Le Thi Lan Khanh, Executive Director of the Children's Advancement Fund, said: "Each sharing always brings many miracles to life. We hope that the "Kite of Hope" festival will bring millions of happy smiles, creating a meaningful summer for all children."

Meaning of Kite Wing - Symbol of hope and miracles

The kite is fragile but powerful, carrying many beautiful meanings in the human soul. It is a symbol of hope, of dreams of flying high and reaching far. When we fly a kite, we put our faith in a bright future and good things to come.

Kite wings are also the miracle of childhood. It carries the laughter and joy of children in the vast sky. Looking at the kite flying high, a magical world opens up, where miracles become reality.

Kites are also a connection between people, a bridge for generous hearts to contribute together for a better life.

title: Join hands to help little Tram completely treat venous malformations
description:
A little girl faces a big challenge

Meet Tram, Tram is a lovely, petite 7-year-old girl, but has to deal with an extremely complicated vein malformation disease. Tram is only a few years old and faces the risk of completely losing her ability to work in the future. Tram lives in a difficult family of 3 people: Tram's mother, Tram's older sister and the baby. Tram's father used to live with his family, but financial pressure due to illness from many sides of his family made him tired and had to live separately from his mother and children. However, sometimes Tram's father still comes home to visit and give gifts to his children, showing that he still cares about his family. Tram's mother is a strong woman who has to work hard to do many jobs such as selling rice, selling fruit,... and is the source of life for her two daughters. Furthermore, Tram's mother recently had a dangerous accident, so she had to switch to lighter jobs such as housework for fear of leaving her two children alone. Compounding the family's difficult situation is Tram's complex vascular malformation, a disease that risks losing Tram's ability to work, causing countless difficulties for her in the future. Therefore, UnityGive requests the help of sponsors to create a medical miracle, changing Tram's life forever.

Severity of venous malformations

Venous malformations occur when the veins in the affected area do not function normally. leading to the veins emerging, becoming more obvious as well as more pain and discomfort in the vein area. Furthermore, the damaged area will become swollen and enlarged, causing the body to become unbalanced. These complications make the baby's hands unable to grasp, causing many difficulties in daily activities. Furthermore, an unusual appearance will put your child at risk of being ostracized in society, making his or her future much more difficult.

The treatment process is full of hope!

Fortunately, with the help of Dr. Luong Ngoc Trung, a senior attending physician at the Department of General, Thoracic and Vascular Surgery at FV Hospital and the support of sponsors through the UnityGive, baby Tram has been receiving the necessary treatment since she came to the Foundation in 2021. Since then, she has received 8 treatments, has healed quite a bit and her hands can now hold objects. Tram's treatment process is reaching its final steps, and she only needs a few more sclerotherapy injections before she can completely heal. However, the high cost of treatment, along with the difficult circumstances of Tram's family, meant that Tram's mother could not pay for her child's complete treatment alone.

Final words

During of operation of the UnityGive Fund, we believe that every person has personal value, needs to be respected and given the opportunity to develop their potential like everyone else, and Tram is no exception. title: Join hands to support living expenses for three especially difficult teenagers in Lao Cai
description:
Unlucky lives in Thai Giang Pho commune

Despite having a very beautiful name - "Mountain of the Rising Sun", Thai Giang Pho commune (Bac Ha district, Lao Cai province) is still in the "war" to eradicate hunger and reduce poverty when the rate of poor and near-poor households of the entire commune reaches 62.37% (According to Lao Cai province's electronic information portal, 2023). With limitations in location, economic conditions and social support, Thai Giang Pho commune still has many unfortunate situations in dire need of attention and support from the community.

Since his mother's death, Vang Seo T. (13 years old) has become even quieter. Due to congenital muteness, T. had previously only stayed at home with his mother. In the past, T. used to go to school, but because of difficult circumstances, his father was in prison for many years, and there were no qualified people around to support him, so T. gradually could not follow and had to drop out of school.

Vang Seo T. by the fire

Then, his mother died suddenly when T was 11 years old, and he moved to live with his uncle's family. Knowing that he is disadvantaged, Mr. Vang Seo A., T.'s uncle, also has to work hard to provide enough food for his family. In the past, T. still communicated by gesturing or talking. But now that my mother is gone, it's hard for my aunt and uncle to understand T., so I'm withdrawing more and more, only my sad eyes seem to speak. Looking at him often loitering alone, Mr. A. shared: "I love him very much, but unfortunately no one in the family understands what he says. Our family also wants him to have a better life."

Women's union officials visited Vang Seo T's family.

Sharing the same situation of being motherless, Vu Thi P. (14 years old) soon learned to help her two uncles take care of her blind father. Besides the state subsidy of 540,000 VND/month, P. and his father no longer have any source of income. Both father and son and his eight family members rely on several crops of corn and rice from the family's small field. Life is even more precarious when you are in your twilight years and your health is no longer as good as before. Loving their niece, they tried to let P. go to school like the other siblings. But because he couldn't concentrate and sometimes kept remembering and forgetting, after a while, P. also quit school and stayed home to help his uncles with work around the house and take care of his father.

Vu Thi P. helps her parents with housework

Luckier than T. and P. because they still have enough loving parents, Chau Seo D. (15 years old) has to endure being bedridden due to congenital lower body paralysis. Even though he was over 15 years old, D.'s legs were as thin and small as those of a ten-year-old child and had no ability to move. So even though he is the oldest brother in the family, D. still needs his parents to take care of him and support him in everything. Even though he couldn't bear to let his child just lie in one place all day, even communicating with only mumbled sounds that no one could understand, Mr. C. (D.'s father), also did not know how to manage when the family was poor, D.'s five siblings still "didn't have enough to eat, didn't have enough to worry about". Therefore, taking D. for treatment or school is a very far-fetched thing.

On weekdays, taking care of D. is hard, but especially when the weather is bad, my whole body feels sharp pain like needles. Sometimes it hurts so much, D. just wants to cry, but because he loves his mother, he tries to suppress the pain. However, D. still maintains his innocence and optimism like a child. Every time he was taken to the yard to sit or had his aunt and uncle visit, D. was so happy, he kept smiling. "My husband and I just wish that D. could live normally, be healthy like other children, know how to dress, walk, eat, etc. In the future, if we receive support, our family would be extremely grateful to the sponsors for caring and helping him ease his hardships," Mr. C. said.

title: Build a green wall along the coast
description:
When nature needs protection...

Along the coastal provinces of the Red River Delta such as Thai Binh, Nam Dinh, Ninh Binh, mangrove forests were once green, used to be a refuge for crabs, fish, storks, and were a natural shield to protect people from storms, floods, and natural disasters. But over time, forests disappear, banks erode, soil salinizes, and fish and shrimp seasons become erratic.

This area is also located in the Red River Delta Biosphere Reserve, recognized by UNESCO since 2004, including two core areas: Xuan Thuy National Park and Tien Hai Wetland Conservation Area - with an area of ​​14,167 hectares, with a typical ecosystem including mangrove forests, tidal flats, and brackish water lagoons. The Red River Biosphere Reserve is also a feeding and migratory place for many waterbirds and migratory birds, with about 200 species of birds, including nearly 60 species of migratory birds and more than 50 species of waterbirds.

Over the past few decades, mangrove forests in the Red River Delta biosphere reserve have been under strong pressure from coastal farming and exploitation activities. In particular, intensive and semi-intensive shrimp farming models have been identified as the leading cause of mangrove loss. The priority for immediate livelihoods has caused many coastal communities to choose to expand shrimp farming areas instead of retaining forests, creating pressure, causing mangrove forests to gradually lose their role as coastal "green shields".

Mangrove forests – not just forest trees

Did you know?

We are taking action – and need your company

Because mangrove restoration cannot be just the work of one organization or one planting season. It is a journey of many years, with patience, responsibility – and above all, faith in nature and people.

title: Stand side by side with me through the flood season
description:
"The damage to people and property keeps increasing every hour, especially many children and students are unable to cope." That is the statement of a local official in Van Tran, Yen Bai.

Typhoon Yagi has been causing heavy damage in many areas in Vietnam, especially the northern mountainous provinces such as Yen Bai, Thai Nguyen, Lao Cai, Tuyen Quang, Hoa Binh, etc. Not only causing floods and heavy rain, the storm also caused landslides, flooding, destroyed people's property, destroyed buildings, but also created great challenges and disadvantages for children and families in difficult circumstances in the highlands. Where living conditions are already difficult, storm season makes the situation even more serious.

3-year-old child was rescued and brought out of the rubble caused by a landslide (Source Lao Cai Newspaper)

According to some quick statistics from the Steering Committee for Natural Disaster Prevention and Search and Rescue - Yen Bai Provincial People's Committee, in Yen Bai, as of September 10, 2024, there were more than 50 casualties, more than 22,000 houses collapsed and damaged, more than 30 schools were flooded, 39 schools had landslides, cracked structures, collapsed fences, and punctured corrugated iron roofs. There were 02 teachers. A member of Yen Bai city died due to a landslide; 7 students died due to the storm.

In Lao Cai, the report of the Lao Cai Steering Committee for Disaster Prevention and Control is also extremely heavy. By September 10, 2024, there were more than 70 casualties, more than 4,000 houses collapsed, 46 communes, 85 villages are isolated, 32 schools were affected by storm damage.

A similar situation also occurs in Tuyen Quang, Hoa Binh, Cao Bang and tends to spread. These are only temporary statistics and may increase in the context of complicated storms. A lot of support and relief has been mobilized, but not just emergency relief. After the storm, with such heavy damage, there is certainly a lot of work to be done, and during the storm or after the storm are equally important.

Landslide broke the window frame in the classroom of Xuan Tam Primary and Secondary School, Van Yen district (Source Yen Bai newspaper)

All 35 houses in Lang Nu village, Phuc Khanh commune were completely buried (Source Lao Cai Newspaper)

Vietnam is one of the six countries most heavily affected by climate change in the world. Climate change is increasingly present most clearly through extreme natural phenomena, causing great and serious damage to communities, especially disadvantaged communities throughout Vietnam. In recent years, we have faced a series of natural problems such as: rain, floods, windstorms, drought, prolonged saltwater intrusion and their severity is increasing. Typhoon Yagi opens the 2024 rainy season, but it is also predicted that more storms could hit the North, Central and South of Vietnam. After each "disaster" passes, it leaves behind severe economic, social and human consequences, negatively impacting the economy and people's lives, especially children: lack of energy, food, clean water, medicine, books, and even physical and mental health. In addition, the timing of natural crises also becomes more irregular and difficult to predict. In every crisis, communities in natural disaster areas, especially children, are always the most vulnerable group due to facing risks and dangers regarding physical, mental, and nutritional health, and especially disruption of access to schools to maintain learning.

That is why we must act together. Pursuing the mission of supporting children's access to education, ensuring comprehensive development and optimizing their potential, and also the Social Fund, social organizations, General Education Innovation Fund (VIGEF) and MSD United Way Vietnam, UnityGive shares the mission with Viettel Money, wishing to call for the community's participation to stand side by side with children in areas affected by storms and natural disasters to overcome storms and floods on the Give now online fundraising platform. We hope to raise funds with an estimated budget of 500,000,000 VND to support children and families in the context of natural disasters, storms and floods. Your contribution can bring:

– Nutritional and epidemiological support packages for disadvantaged families; – Packages of clothes, shoes, books and school supplies for children to go to school; – Support for schools in renovating facilities and equipment to ensure learning and return to school for students after the storm and flood season; – Educational activities and awareness raising on prevention and mitigation of natural disasters and climate change in schools; – Other post-crisis recovery and reconstruction support packages as needed reality.

title: 2,000 meals for people in need at Quan Yen Vui

Up to now, the Fund has 8 Happy Yen Restaurants in: Hanoi, Nghe An, Quang Tri, Da Nang, Gia Lai, Khanh Hoa, Can Tho and An Giang.

Who are the guests of Quan Yen Vui?

For the 2000 VND Rice Restaurant system, we do not differentiate between customers, we call them essential people. However, the shop's regular customers are street workers such as lottery ticket sellers, waste pickers, motorbike taxi drivers, street vendors... These are people with unstable income, fluctuating between 100-200 VND/day. In big city areas, their lives face many difficulties.

Street workers often move on the road, not permanently, and eating and drinking are often not taken care of. They will eat and drink temporarily with food they bring or food sold on the roadside. These meals often do not ensure food hygiene and safety, and are insufficient in quantity and quality.

Street workers often only have health as a source of capital. However, eating poorly and having to work too hard will lead to illness in the long run.

Street workers often do not receive good services. Difficulties in life make them sensitive and vulnerable subjects. Sometimes they lose faith in kindness. What they lack is not only a material meal, but also a good service attitude, and belief in the good things in life.

What do we have at Quan Yen Fun?

Yen Vui Restaurant provides meals that ensure food hygiene and safety, are nutritious and delicious. To do that, Yen Vui prepares meals at a processing facility that ensures food hygiene and safety, kitchen staff receive regular health checks, and have sample storage cabinets...

A lunch includes: rice, main dish, side dish (stir-fried), soup and dessert. Rice is served unlimitedly, to ensure everyone is full enough to continue working. On average, each Yen Vui restaurant will serve 200-300 meals/day and 3 days/week.

We encourage guests to dine at the restaurant for a comfortable space and attentive service. Yen Vui does not donate charity meals, but provides cheap meals with respect for customers. For each meal, the symbolic price is 1,000 VND - 2,000 VND. We hope that with each meal, people can save money for other more urgent living expenses: school fees for children, daily medicine costs, electricity bills or at least have an afternoon meal. Many people only eat one meal a day, 1 portion of rice divided into 2 meals, stop taking medicine to save money for their children to go to school...

Yen Vui not only provides cheap meals or necessary support, but also the invisible things. Like belief in goodness, love for life, taste of shared joy...

In addition to providing cheap meals, Yen Vui is also an extended arm of the Lotus Charity Foundation to carry out charity projects outside Ho Chi Minh City to bring benefits to people in need such as supporting difficult circumstances in highland and remote areas, promptly implementing emergency relief programs such as natural disasters, epidemics, etc.

title: Bringing the Tet of Hope to people in the Dak Lak floodplain
description:
After the historic flood in November, the small house of Mr. Nguyen Xuan Quang, 72 years old, Tuy An Dong commune, Dak Lak was still filled with sadness because of the pain of losing a loved one - his son, Mr. Nguyen Xuan Khanh, 42 years old. On the day of the accident, Mr. Khanh went to pick up his relatives while the floodwaters were rising. The current was too strong and swept away the entire group of four people, three people died (including two grandchildren). Mr. Khanh is the breadwinner of his family including his wife and two children, of which the eldest son is mentally disabled. His passing makes family life even more difficult, and we don't know how to manage it.

Hoa Thinh residents repaired their roofs after the flood. Photo: Thanh Tung

People in Dak Lak lost their homes after storms and floods in November

Unlike Mr. Quang's family, which lost relatives, Mr. Ho Van Giac's family lost all their assets when their two houses - including his house and the house of his daughter and her husband - were completely collapsed and their furniture was also swept away. After the flood, the whole family just built a temporary tarpaulin roof to shelter from the rain and sun. In recent days, his family has received support from the army to build a house to stabilize soon, but there are still hundreds of worries surrounding him when starting life again from scratch, and Tet is near.

On the morning of November 23, many trucks carrying goods entered the flood zone of Hoa Thinh commune, Dak Lak to supply food, clothes, and necessities. Photo: Dinh Van

People in flood areas lined up to receive supplies.

Mr. Tran Van Bien - Chairman of Tuy An Dong Commune People's Committee, said that the historic flood killed 12 people, a too large number for this purely agricultural commune; More than 10,000 houses were flooded, dozens of households had their houses collapsed and were seriously damaged.

"People were completely caught off guard because the floods rose quickly and flowed rapidly, causing many houses to collapse; livestock and poultry were almost lost. 13/14 villages of the commune were deeply flooded, the damage was very heavy and people faced many difficulties," Mr. Bien said. Total damage is estimated at more than 1,500 billion VND.

Dak Lak (formerly Phu Yen) was flooded with thousands of houses

Tuy An Dong is one of the communes that suffered the most damage during the historic flood in Dak Lak in November. And Dak Lak is also the province that suffered the heaviest damage in the South Central region with 113 people lost due to floods. To this day, the obsession is still there - the image of the vast ocean, the feeling of helplessness when a lifetime's effort is swept away and the insecurity when the Lunar New Year is approaching...

Bringing Tet Hope to share love

In order to bring a warm and loving Tet season to the people in the Tuy An Dong floodplain, the Hope Foundation wishes to carry out the Tet of Hope program. Each Tet gift is not only practical support, but also a lighted fire of hope, opening the door to a brighter new year after losses caused by natural disasters.

Give gifts to people in flooded areas

The 2026 Tet of Hope program is expected to give 1,000 Tet gifts to households damaged by storms and floods; Poor and near-poor households in Tuy An Dong commune, Dak Lak. Each gift includes essential necessities, Tet items and cash, worth 1.5-2.5 million VND, helping families ease difficulties and have more conditions for a warmer Tet.

Every contribution, no matter how small, contributes to bringing a fuller Tet and gives more motivation and spread love so that people can gradually stabilize their lives after natural disasters.

title: Bua Coc - a resettled village after a historic flood needs a school
description:
After the terrible flood and landslide that occurred at the end of 2017, causing heavy damage to people and property, people in Coi 1, Coi 2, Coi 3 hamlets of Nanh Nghe commune (Da Bac district, Hoa Binh province) were relocated by the government to new places to avoid repeating natural disasters. 70 households gathered in the resettlement village with the new name Bua Coc.

The new life of the households has gradually stabilized after more than 5 years of resettlement, but many difficulties still remain. Children still lack on-site classes…

Historic flood

Prolonged heavy rain from October 9 to 11, 2017 caused water levels to rise in underground areas, and Provincial Road 433 collapsed in many places; 14 highland communes of Da Bac district, Hoa Binh were divided and isolated. Floods and flash floods in many communes left 11 people dead and missing; 50 houses collapsed and were completely swept away; 325 houses were eroded, many roads and bridges were seriously damaged.

Suoi Nanh commune (now Nanh Nghe commune after merging Suoi Nanh and Dong Nghe communes) is the most severely affected commune. Particularly, the flood on the night of October 10, 2017 caused 5 people living in the Ngam Ruoc area to drift away and go missing; 10 houses in Coi hamlet were completely destroyed along with hundreds of houses partially damaged, etc. v. Households that suffered damage and were at high risk of landslides in the commune were relocated by the government to new places to ensure safety.

The new resettlement village still faces many difficulties

Bua Coc is one of two resettlement hamlets for people affected by the historic flood of 2017 in Nanh Nghe commune. Most of the people in Bua Coc hamlet lived in Coi 1, Coi 2, and Coi 3 hamlets before moving. The resettlement area - the new hamlet is about 8km from the people's old residence.

Even though the state invested in building infrastructure, provided residential land, farmland, and financial support to stabilize a new life in the early days of resettlement, however, the lives of 70 households with 269 people from the Muong and Tay ethnic groups in Bua Coc hamlet still face many difficulties.

The entire hamlet still has 28.6% of poor households and 44.3% of near-poor households. Lack of arable land while the economy depends mainly on gardening - forestry, lack of clean water, some locations around the hamlet with landslides are the things that people in Bua Coc hamlet are facing.

In particular, children in the neighborhood have to travel dozens of kilometers to go to school every day because the neighborhood does not have a school for primary school or higher.

Join hands to build Bua Coc school

Understanding the difficulties of Bua Coc people in general and school-aged children in particular, the Foundation for Vietnamese Stature has coordinated with the National Volunteer Center, Hoa Binh Provincial Youth Union and Da Bac District Youth Union to call and mobilize resources to build a school for children in Bua Coc hamlet. Once completed, the school site will be one of the schools under the management of Suoi Nanh Primary and Secondary School.

The school site with 2 classrooms will have an estimated construction cost of about 345,000,000 VND.

Initially, responding to the call from the For Vietnamese Stature Fund and other parties, Youth Union members of Bac A Commercial Joint Stock Bank responded and contributed an amount of 270,000,000 VND. Compared to the total estimated cost to build this school, it is still 75,000,000 VND short.

We hope to receive the cooperation of the UnityGive community and Viettel Pay users, who are kind-hearted and care about the education of children in Bua Coc, to have enough money of 345,000,000 VND to build a safe, clean, beautiful and spacious school for children in this village.

title: Together support the construction of a kindergarten for Ban Mong ethnic students, Son Thuy commune, Quan Son district, Thanh Hoa province
description:
Mong village kindergarten in Son Thuy commune, Quan Son district, Thanh Hoa province is a school with a large number of students and high learning needs. Mong village has nearly 80 kindergarten and primary school students, including nearly 60 children who have reached preschool age. However, the physical conditions cannot be met, so many children still do not go to school and they do not have access to quality education.

Ban Mong is a village close to the Vietnam - Laos border (about 2km as the crow flies), about 24km from the headquarters of the People's Committee of Son Thuy commune (it takes about 3 hours to move from the commune center to the school). Because this is a border village, the roads are extremely difficult to travel, most of them are slippery dirt roads. On rainy days, traffic is completely cut off and it is impossible to travel. The entire village has nearly 70 households, of which 100% are poor and near-poor households. The people in the village are all Mong people, so the new village is called Mong village. The families' main occupation is farming or going to the forest to gather, so their income is low and unstable. People here always understand that going to school to learn letters and knowledge is the only way to escape poverty.

The kindergarten in Mong village currently has more than 30 students (meeting 50% of the school's needs) due to not having enough classrooms. Currently, the children are having to study in temporary classrooms built from wooden planks assembled into walls a long time ago (about more than 20 years), with an area of ​​about 40 m2, the planks have deteriorated a lot due to termites and bad effects of weather, and the cement floor has deteriorated. The roof is made of small flat-cut boards put together, so on rainy and windy days, water will flow inside, making it impossible for children to study.

To accompany the local government and school students on the path of learning and conquering intellectual dreams, the Capital Volunteer Club in conjunction with the Youth Union of the Central Youth Union would like to call on the social community, companies and businesses to join hands to donate 200,000,000 VND in cash to support the rebuilding of the Mong village kindergarten. Leaving school, young man Nguyen Quang Chien followed the Party's call to join the army in August 1985. When the war in Vi Xuyen was fierce, he was assigned to E876F356. Three years of living fighting and serving in Thanh Thuy, Vi Xuyen district, Ha Giang province, many comrades of the same age stayed in this land. He was lucky to return alive...

Returning to everyday life in the countryside of Tuy Loc commune, bordering Yen Bai city, there were few fields and no jobs, so he worked hard to do all kinds of jobs hoping that one day life would get better... But life for him was not smooth, 4 years after leaving the army he was sick all the time, sciatica had been with him for nearly ten years, his parents' house was very poor and there were many brothers, so his family's difficulties became even more difficult.

At the age of 45, he first got married to Hien, his wife. Since getting married, his health has gradually stabilized. The couple enjoys staying up late and waking up early with the milling machine that their parents saved up to buy before moving out. When his and his wife's life was gradually stabilizing, in 2015 he discovered he had colon cancer. For three consecutive years, he went from one hospital to another. Anh's wife worked hard day and night to take care of her husband. Whatever money she had saved, she used all the medicine for him. When his health was temporarily stable, it was her turn to have a stroke and require brain surgery. After 9 months in the hospital in Hanoi, their house had nothing of value left. There were a few acres of fields that he and his wife had to sell, then borrowed money from friends, family, and relatives to help.

She returned home with a crippled hand and spasms, having to use a cane to take small steps to be able to walk...for five years now, since she had a stroke, all family matters have worried about the family's medication falling on him, while he still has to check for colon cancer every three months. His family life was already difficult, but now it is even more difficult.

The wooden house his family built for him and his wife for 15 years is now seriously degraded. The cement roof has leaked in many places. He had to use a tarpaulin to temporarily cover it. The hope of having a small house with a corrugated iron roof so that an elderly and sick couple can rely on each other is so far away...

With this story, we, the old comrades of the F356 Veteran, call on our comrades and the community to join hands in building him and his wife a warm, small house.

title: Walk with me through storm Yagi, for a resilient Vietnam
description:
Typhoon Yagi just "swept" the Northern provinces of Vietnam on September 6-7, 2024 and has weakened into a tropical depression but continues with heavy rains capable of causing flooding in low-lying areas; Flash floods on small rivers and streams, landslides on steep slopes. The damages are still being calculated, but the impact is certainly not small. MSD United Way Vietnam does not want to sit and wait, we want to immediately prepare to take action to support children and families affected by Typhoon Yagi in particular and floods in Vietnam in general through the fundraising campaign "Let's walk through the flood season with you, for a resilient Vietnam".

…..

Vietnam is one of the six countries most heavily affected by climate change in the world. Climate change is increasingly present most clearly through extreme natural phenomena, causing great and serious damage to communities, especially disadvantaged communities throughout Vietnam. In recent years, we have faced a series of natural problems such as: rain, floods, windstorms, drought, prolonged saltwater intrusion and their severity is increasing. After each "disaster" passes, it leaves behind severe economic, social and human consequences, negatively impacting the economy and people's lives. In addition, the timing of natural crises also becomes more irregular and difficult to predict. In every crisis, communities in natural disaster areas, especially children, are always the most vulnerable group due to facing risks and dangers regarding physical, mental, and nutritional health, and especially disruption of access to schools to maintain learning.

In recent years, MSD United Way Vietnam, through the For a Resilient Vietnam initiative, has focused on mobilizing resources to contribute to supporting local communities when emergency situations occur (such as COVID 19, storms, prolonged floods, etc.). To date, we have provided nutritional, medical, and educational support to more than 5,000 people in emergency situations. Realizing that, in order to be able to provide timely support to prevent, avoid and minimize the consequences of natural crises for vulnerable communities, especially children in remote and vulnerable areas during and after storms and floods, early preparation of resources and solutions is required.

One student also shared: "I really want to go to school regularly and not have to worry about storms. Many times, my friends and I have to stay home because we can't go to school. I hope to have more books and learning tools and hope that the way to school will be safer." These shared words clearly demonstrate the desire for a brighter future, with stable living and learning conditions for students and teachers in the highlands.

Therefore, MSD United Way Vietnam wishes to call for the participation of the community, individuals, and organizations to contribute urgently and or regularly to this project/initiative of ours so that when an emergency situation such as Typhoon Yagi occurs, we can promptly assist the community, minimize difficulties and losses, and overcome the consequences of the emergency situation. Support packages under the initiative Together with you through the flood season - For a resilient Vietnam are expected to include, but are not limited to:

– Nutritional and epidemiological support package for disadvantaged families – Support package to ensure access and maintenance of uninterrupted learning – Communication activities, raising awareness on prevention and mitigation of natural disasters and climate change. – Support package for recovery and reconstruction after the crisis.

Currently, we are raising emergency funds to help overcome the effects of Typhoon Yagi on difficult and vulnerable children and families in the path of the storm. The new school year has just begun, we do not expect any children to have their studies interrupted or have to stop going to school due to the impact of Typhoon Yagi. We are urgently collecting statistics on cases that need support and continuously updating, the estimated emergency fundraising budget is 150,000,000 VND.

A timely support will bring positive changes to the lives of vulnerable children, helping them have a strong and bright present and future.

title: “Growing Together With You” raises funds to sponsor boarding meals for children in highland areas
description:
Bao Lam district, Cao Bang province is a district located in a particularly difficult area of ​​Cao Bang province, almost all of the population are H'Mong and Dao ethnic people, belonging to poor and near-poor households.

However, in the middle of rolling mountains, each commune, separated by several mountains, has many preschools, with teachers who persevere in the village and children who are eager to learn and yearn to go to school. The children do not hesitate to cross mountains, wade streams, and walk on rough, rocky forest roads to go to school every day.

Two years ago, the school bags of nearly 200 highland children only had a handful of men men (traditional dish of the H'Mong people) or a little plain white rice mixed with spring water, not enough to fill their stomachs. Many children suffer from malnutrition, especially stunting.

Their difficulties are not only that, on hot summer days, their lunches are easily spoiled, so sometimes they have to share food with other friends or have to walk several kilometers through the forest (about 40-50 minutes) to get home for lunch. This greatly affects the attendance rate of students, when up to 80% of students go home at noon without returning to school.

Starting from the 2020-2021 school year, the Vietnamese Stature Foundation (VSF) has launched the project "Growing with children" to sponsor boarding meals for about 200 preschool students at 2 schools Khau Noong and Na O under Thach Lam Kindergarten, and 3 schools Khau De, Sang Soay, Ban La under Thai Son Kindergarten.

After two years of implementation, the "Growing Together" Project has sponsored a total of nearly 120,000 nutritious boarding meals (including lunch and afternoon snacks) for nearly 400 preschool students in Bao Lam district, Cao Bang province. Nutritious lunches with rice, meat, fish, vegetables, fruits; Special snacks with vermicelli, porridge, noodles, etc. v. has provided children with balanced nutrition, helping them have more health to study. At the same time, boarding meals are also a motivation for children to go to school. Thanks to adequate nutrition, after one school year, more than 90% of children gain weight and height significantly after one school year, with an average increase of 1.7kg in weight and 2.9cm in height (data for the 2021-2022 school year).

In addition to providing nutritious boarding meals for students, the project also helps improve learning conditions for students such as: Installing solar batteries, equipping clean water systems, kitchen utensils, water purifiers, refrigerators, blankets and foam for nap areas. Every year, the project also organizes a volunteer trip to hand out warm winter coats, school bags, rain boots, toys, books, etc. with the desire to further motivate and encourage the children on their journey through the mountains and passes to go to school.

Nearly 3 years later, with the help of the local government and neighbors, the couple was able to rebuild a small wooden house with a cement tile roof. I thought life would go on smoothly...

While in the army, he was injured but has not been evaluated. At the end of 1992, he sent the certificate of injury to the District Team to wait for the District to implement the policy for Invalids... But before the documents could be completed, suddenly while working as a hired laborer, he had an accident at work... and died at the end of 1993.

He left behind his young wife, his old mother and two preschool-aged children, everything fell on his sister-in-law's thin shoulders... Life went on like that, the two children had grown up with the love and care of their mother and neighbors, but because of their poor circumstances, they had not completed their secondary school education yet, so they dropped out of school and worked as hired laborers to help the family.

In July 2018, a historic flood swept through the village, dozens of roofs were swept away or collapsed. After many years of saving, her family's assets were swept away by the flood... After the flood, the local government and benefactors helped her build a round wooden house made of forest trees. Now, after 5 years, the house has seriously deteriorated. The pillars and beams were damaged by termites, and the walls on both gables had collapsed, so she had to cover them with a tarpaulin.

We visited the family and could not imagine that this was a family. She was only 60 years old but she looked as miserable as if she were 70. There was nothing worth money in the house except an old refrigerator that I bought at a second-hand store. She confided that she only wished to have the opportunity to rebuild a house to have peace of mind in her old age, but it was too difficult. Now she suffers from osteoarthritis and sciatica and only stays at home while her 1 child, who is not yet married, works as a hired laborer to earn money for her and her child's living expenses. The family has been near poverty for many years but cannot escape poverty...

title: Donating bricks to build a school for students in Na Tau, Son La
description:
At around 5 p.m., Song Thi Pa Teach (10 years old, Dea Mon commune, Song Ma district, Son La) carried her bag out of the classroom, waiting for her 2nd grade sister to return to the dormitory with her. Pa Tach and her sister are Mong ethnic people, studying at Na Tau school of Dea Mon Primary School, Song Ma district.

The room, about 6 m2 in size, with three pieces of wood stacked together to make a bed, is the residence of two sisters and four other female students, about 16 m from the school. Under the bed was filled with pre-cut dry firewood, brought down from the mountain by the children's parents. Quickly taking off his coat, Pa Teaching poured rice into a cast iron pot and washed it. Quickly with her hands, she carried the firewood to the stove and built a fire to cook.

Students attending Na Tau School, Dua Mon Commune Primary School, cook their own meals in their dorm rooms.

In the makeshift kitchen, students placed their own iron bars to make the stove. Just like that, 5-6 pots of rice turned red at the same time. When the rice boiled, Pa Duy boiled water to mix instant noodles and eggs, along with some vegetables to make soup. This is my regular menu. A few days a week, I have dried fish or some pork sent by my parents.

Na Tau school is located in Dea Mon commune, a particularly difficult third-region commune, 45 km from the center of Song Ma district, Son La province. The terrain here is mainly hills and mountains with 21 villages of Thai, Mong, Kho Mu people... Of about 1,700 households, more than half are poor and near-poor households (per capita income is less than 1.5 million VND a month).

Song Thi Pa Teaching (white shirt) and her friends in the motel room.

Currently, the whole school has 149 students, of which 82 students are eligible for a boarding regime of about 600,000 VND for meals, nearly 150,000 VND for rent per month, and rent their own houses around the school. Children whose homes are 2.5 km or more away from the school, where the roads are slippery and cannot be returned during the day, are given 15 kg of rice monthly. Mr. Tong Van Hoai, Principal of Dea Mon Primary School, said: "Because the school is small and lacking, the school cannot open a boarding kitchen, so it is forced to let the children take care of their own food every day," Mr. Hoai said.

Prefabricated classroom at Na Tau school.

Currently, Na Tau students are studying in 5 assembled classrooms, the space is not enough for students to study. Meanwhile, the two teachers' living rooms were temporarily made of wood and roofed with roofing sheets made by the villagers themselves and put into use since 2003. They are currently degraded, severely damaged, and unsafe. The temporary toilet is old and worn out.

Teacher's wooden house at Na Tau school.

Mr. Nguyen Cong Vien, Head of the Department of Education and Training of Song Ma district, said that the district Department of Education and schools along with organizations and individuals have many programs to support clothes, school supplies, and food for Na Tau students. However, teachers and students still have many difficulties. "In the long term, in order for students here to study with peace of mind, we hope that the government, organizations and individuals will continue to pay attention to investing in facilities," Mr. Vien said.

title: Join hands to support cancer treatment costs for Vietnamese children
description:
The cancer boy's dream of raising his mother

Viet once promised he would take care of his mother when she gets old, but now the 13-year-old boy is lying in a hospital bed, whispering, "If I can't stand it anymore, what should I do?".

More than a year ago, Nguyen Tien Viet was diagnosed with a mediastinal malignant tumor located between the heart and lungs. He had surgery in mid-2022, but now the tumor continues to grow.

"The doctor said the tumor grows back too quickly. Now it can last a day or a day," said Vietnamese mother, Pham Thi Phuong (42 years old) in Phu Minh village, Ky Phu commune, Ky Anh district, Ha Tinh province.

Viet grew up with his mother and two older siblings in a house with a low corrugated iron roof, scorching hot summers, and cutting colds. When he was two years old, his father disappeared at sea after only three months of going to Korea to export labor, leaving behind his wife and small child and a debt of 400 million VND.

To raise her children and pay off her debt, Ms. Phuong has to wake up at 4 a.m., ride her bike to the beach to collect crabs and fish, and then cycle back to the market to sell. On many days, the mother of three children earns 100,000 VND, but on stormy days she returns empty-handed. In the afternoon, she alone worked with two acres of rice fields. When there is a good harvest, we have enough to eat, but when there is a bad harvest, we have to carry baskets and ask for rice from our grandmother's house.

The mother initially determined to work hard to bring the best life for her children, but Viet's illness destroyed her plans.

"I'm not a good mother. If I didn't work all day, I could have detected my child's illness earlier without waiting so long," she blamed herself.

Viet's illness actually lasted a while. At the time of discovery, the tumor had invaded the mediastinum between the heart and lungs. The only thing that can be done is surgical resection and chemotherapy to maintain life. The family had no money, so relatives and neighbors gathered 20 million enough for the surgery. Food and living expenses for mother and child during treatment at the Oncology Department, Hue Central Hospital had to be borrowed or asked for charity.

To treat his illness, Viet quit school after finishing 6th grade. Before that, his mother had prepared a convincing argument why he could not continue to go to school, but the boy did not stop crying.

Like other children his age, Viet likes to play soccer. But after being treated for nearly two years in the hospital, Viet seemed to turn into a different person. Most of the day, he stared blankly at the empty space in front of him, not even wanting to get out of bed.

"Partly because of fatigue, partly because Viet feels sorry for herself when her friends go to school, have parents to pick them up and take care of them, but her children do not," Ms. Phuong said.

Every three months of treatment, mother and daughter return home for a few days. The first thing when Viet entered the house was to light incense on his father's altar and clasp his hands together to pray. The boy still hopes for a miracle so he can continue to go to school and that his life is not just tied to his hospital bed.

Every time she looked at her child respectfully before the altar, Ms. Phuong's eyes turned red. This woman couldn't count how many times she cried since her son fell ill. But the tears that fall the most are when Viet cries, "Mom, I can't bear it anymore."

Those were the times when chemotherapy vomited all day, and I had to have someone to help me wherever I went. Even the simplest movements can exhaust him. When hearing the news that the tumor had grown back just half a year after surgery, Viet held his mother's hand and asked: "Can we go home? I don't want to be in the hospital anymore."

To encourage, Ms. Phuong often clasped her son's thin hands, covered in stings from his injections, against her cheeks, whispering: "For mom, please try harder."

This saying was used many times and Viet still persisted in staying at the hospital according to her mother's wishes. However, the longer the treatment time, the more this family's worries about food and money pile up.

"This is a patient with a particularly difficult family background. Although the hospital has spent a lot of gifts and money to support it, it can only partially share the burden," said Ms. Truong Kim Yen, head nurse of the Oncology Department, Hue Central Hospital.

According to the female nurse, Viet is currently continuing chemotherapy to prevent new tumors from growing. If there are signs of atrophy, surgery will not be required. In the remaining cases, surgery costs will be a big burden on the family's economy.

Even though there are still many difficulties ahead, Ms. Phuong always tries to get her child treated according to the doctor's orders. "I will do everything I can to help Viet stay with her mother as long as possible," she said.

As for Viet, even though he doesn't know if he can fulfill his promise to his mother, there is one thing the 13-year-old boy can be sure of: having a mother is the greatest blessing in life.

Because the scar cannot keep up with the body's growth, it causes the elbow to contract and cannot straighten, while the elbow experiences contracture. Furthermore, because the baby is still young and hyperactive, his vigorous movements run the risk of cracking and ulcerating the wound. Fortunately, Thao will receive treatment support from Dr. Tran Anh Tan, who has 17 years of experience in burn scar surgery. Before that, the child's family had to borrow money from family to pay hospital fees. Even though they have enough income to get by, the child's family does not have money for emergencies. This makes the child's family unable to pay for treatment.

At the Raising Children's Charity Foundation, our greatest joy is when we see the smiles on children's faces when they know their injuries will soon end. This is what every child in the world deserves, a chance to reach their full potential. Therefore, we believe that every contribution, no matter how big or small, helps Thao get closer to a future where she has the opportunity to live a healthy and happy life. Together, let's help Thao get the treatment she needs so she can keep her bright smile in the future.

title: Improve wood stoves - Contribute to preserving forests
description:
In Van Ho commune, Van Ho district, Son La province, there is a strip of natural forest with an area of ​​1,175 hectares in 4 villages: Bo Nhang 2, Pa Cop, Chua Tai and Hua Tat, located on a limestone mountain range at an altitude of 1,300 to 1,600 meters. This forest strip is adjacent to Hang Kia - Pa Co Nature Reserve (Hoa Binh province) and shares the same landscape with Xuan Nha Nature Reserve. Although located outside the existing special-use forests and strongly affected by the socio-economic activities of local people, Van Ho natural forest still retains many unique natural values, providing an important source of non-timber forest products and wood for households in the village to use in daily life.

Women are in charge of collecting firewood and cooking in the family

Among the four villages, Pa Cop has the largest number of poor households (nearly 40%), most of whom are H'Mong people. People here have maintained the habit of using firewood for many generations to cook, heat, dry food for storage, and boil fabric to make clothes. Traditional wood stoves use iron brackets placed on firewood, which often cannot control indoor smoke and dust and poses a high risk of fire and explosion during the dry season. This type of stove can only utilize 10-15% of the heat generated, so it wastes a lot of firewood. It is estimated that a household can use up to 10 m3 of firewood a year, especially in the 3 months of Tet, it can consume up to 5 m3 of firewood, putting considerable pressure on the increasingly depleted forest wood resources. Responsibility for collecting firewood (heavy baskets) and cooking often falls to women, so women face higher health risks.

Wood-saving stoves help reduce the amount of firewood burned by up to 60%.

According to actual surveys, using a wood-saving stove can help reduce up to 60% of the amount of firewood, save up to 35% of the time spent gathering firewood, lighting the stove and cooking, and has less smoke and dust than traditional stoves, thus reducing lung and respiratory diseases, limiting the risk of fire and labor accidents, and taking advantage of many types of fuel and agricultural by products. Each family using an improved stove can save up to 1.5 tons of firewood per year, equivalent to the coverage of a large forest area. Supporting people in Pa Cop to get acquainted, build and use wood-saving stoves will contribute significantly to forest protection, improve the environment, improve quality of life and reduce dependence on forests, maintaining a harmonious relationship between people and nature.

Funds called for from the UnityGive platform will support at least 50% of the most difficult households to access and use wood-saving stoves, change resource use behavior, and serve as a driving force for change for the remaining households in the village. At the same time, the capital also supports propaganda activities for people about wood-saving stoves, integrating knowledge about the environment and forest protection. Communication activities and support for building wood stoves will be carried out in July and August 2022.

title: Join hands to help Mr. Dang Ton Pu regain his light
description:
Mr. Dang Ton Pu (1991), a Dao ethnic person in the border commune of Ia Rve (Ea Sup district, Dak Lak province) has neurofibromatosis syndrome that causes facial deformities. Currently, one eye has been completely blinded by a broken eyeball, the other eye is also being filled with tumors, and his vision is only 2/10. He is the third child in a poor farmer family of four children. At the age of 10, Pu's parents sent him to first grade school. But after only reaching third grade, Pu began to get sick. Large tumors appeared all over his face, and small pimples also appeared on his body. At the hospital, the doctor said Pu unfortunately had neurofibromatosis syndrome, a rare disease that is difficult to treat. Being discriminated against and shunned by his friends, Pu felt sorry for himself and quit school, staying at home to work the land and help his parents farm. His mother died early, his father got married elsewhere, and now Mr. Pu lives alone in a torn house, working every day to make a living. The neighbors felt sorry for him in his misfortune, and if he had any work to do, they would call him to do it and pay him. Many times the sharp pain continued to torment him, but Mr. Pu did not have money to buy medicine. title: Help baby Minh Quan hear the sounds of life
description:
Pham Minh Quan, 6 years old, currently lives with his family in village 16, Ea Wer commune, Dak Lak province. Right from birth, he had no ear flaps or ears on both sides - a birth defect that made him unable to hear and speak.

His parents are Mr. Pham Quoc Bao (born in 1990) and Ms. Pham Bich Quyen (born in 1991), Dao ethnic people, in particularly difficult circumstances. Mr. Bao works far away from home to make a living, while Ms. Quyen stays home to take care of her two small children. Even though they tried to take their child to the doctor and borrowed from many places to find treatment opportunities, the family still could not cover the costs.

Through examination, the doctor diagnosed that if equipped with a specialized hearing aid, Minh Quan could improve his hearing, start learning to speak and gradually integrate into life. However, the cost for suitable support equipment is up to about 80 million VND, which is too large a number for the family at this time.

Faced with the above situation, Tu Tam Dak Lak Fund calls on the community, charitable organizations and individuals to join hands to help so that Quan has the opportunity to hear and go to school like other children.
